summary: Discovery focused on Luminex's security and compliance requirements for choosing between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private Redwood deployments. Key points: SOC2/ISO attestation needed, SSO via SAML required, granular RBAC and audit logs mandatory, KMS integration and customer-managed keys desired for Private/Dedicated, and data retention/ERasure policies. Agreed next steps: share compliance docs, SAML guide, schedule dedicated scoping call, customer to share network diagram.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-06
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Jesse Carter (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Paul Chen (CTO, Luminex), Sara Vogel (Head of Security), Daniel Ortiz (DevOps)

[00:00] Jesse Carter: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Jesse on the AE side, with Maya our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Paul Chen: Hey Jesse, thanks. We appreciate you fitting us in, a few folks on our side are juggling meetings.
[00:12] Sara Vogel: Sara here, head of security. We'll be focused on compliance and data controls.
[00:16] Maya Singh: Great. High level, is this a pure security posture run or do you want a little product fit as well?
[00:21] Paul Chen: Mainly security today. We're evaluating Redwood for inference — considering hosted for speed but Dedicated or Private for data residency and key controls.
[00:30] Jesse Carter: Makes sense. Today we'll cover SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC/audit logs, encryption and KMS, and retention/erasure. Then propose next steps.

[04:02] Maya Singh: On SOC2, Redwood is SOC2 Type II (note: spelling in our notes says S-O-C two) — we can share the attestation PDF. For ISO we have 27001 in process, we can provide scope.
[04:20] Sara Vogel: Good. We need formal attestation for our vendor review. Also any penetration test summaries and third-party risk assessments?
[04:30] Jesse Carter: Yep, we have a security pack — pen test summaries and an executive SOC report. I'll attach that after the call.

[08:05] Daniel Ortiz: From infra, main blockers are VPC peering and whether we can bring our own KMS. If we go hosted we need customer-managed keys or at least envelope encryption.
[08:18] Maya Singh: For Hosted we support customer key wrap via KMS integrations; for Dedicated/Private you can bring your own KMS/HSM. There's some nuance with key rotation and how long KV cache is stored — sorry, I said KV cash earlier in notes — the KV cache is ephemeral but logs are encrypted.
[08:32] Paul Chen: When you say "bring your own KMS", is that full key control? We can't have provider access to raw keys.
[08:37] Maya Singh: For Private, yes you manage keys in your cloud KMS or on-prem HSM, Redwood doesn't retain plaintext. For Dedicated there are options to restrict key access; we can show the architecture diagram.

[12:10] Sara Vogel: SSO — SAML is mandatory for us. We need SCIM for provisioning and ability to enforce MFA via our IdP.
[12:21] Jesse Carter: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. We also have RBAC with role templates; you can map SAML groups to roles.
[12:30] Daniel Ortiz: Any limit on role granularity? We need per-team model access control and audit events for token-level usage.
[12:38] Maya Singh: You can create custom roles and map groups; audit logs capture per-token activity, request metadata, and model/version used. Logs can be exported to your SIEM via syslog/S3.

[17:50] Paul Chen: How long do you retain logs and data by default, and can we set retention policies? Also GDPR/data erasure concerns.
[17:58] Jesse Carter: Default retention is 90 days for full logs, 365 days for metadata in some tiers, but retention is configurable on Dedicated/Private. For Hosted we offer custom retention add-ons. We can support data erasure requests and provide deletion confirmations.

[21:05] Sara Vogel: Wanted to confirm audit trail integrity — are logs tamper-evident? Do you support append-only storage or signed logs?
[21:14] Maya Singh: We provide immutable storage for audit records in Dedicated/Private; for Hosted we use write-once storage and can provide signed attestations on request. We'll include specifics in the security pack.

[25:01] Daniel Ortiz: Network — we need to know about egress controls, private endpoints, and VPC peering setup. Is there a managed transit or do we set up peering and route tables?
[25:12] Maya Singh: For Private deployments, you control the VPC and can run the control plane in your VPC. For Dedicated we offer VPC peering and private endpoints; our ops team helps with route tables. We'll need your network diagram.

[29:30] Paul Chen: Performance tradeoffs — our product needs sub-200ms p50 for short prompts in some flows. If we choose Dedicated, can we guarantee latency?
[29:40] Jesse Carter: Dedicated gives predictable throughput and SLA-backed latency targets; we'll run a bench with your typical prompts. If latency is critical we can prioritize colocated capacity. We'll share the benchmark template.

[33:05] Sara Vogel: Encryption at rest and in transit — AES-256, TLS 1.2/1.3? Key derivation specifics?
[33:13] Maya Singh: Yes TLS 1.2+ and TLS 1.3 supported. At rest we use AES-256 with customer-managed KMS options. For Dedicated/Private you can use your KMS/HSM and control rotation policies.

[36:40] Daniel Ortiz: Any concerns about model data leakage — e.g., does Redwood store prompts used for caching or are they ephemeral?
[36:48] Maya Singh: We do automatic prefix/KV caching to improve performance but you can opt-out or control cache TTL. For sensitive workloads we recommend Private with no external cache or configure per-route caching rules. We'll document caching behavior in the security notes.

[40:12] Paul Chen: Are there attestations or third-party certs for our compliance program beyond SOC2? You mentioned ISO27001 in progress — timeline?
[40:20] Jesse Carter: ISO27001 cert expected Q3; we'll share the scope and status. We also have third-party vulnerability assessments.

[43:00] Sara Vogel: Ok recap then next steps please.
[43:05] Jesse Carter: Recap — we'll send SOC2/ISO docs, pen test summaries, SAML/SCIM guide, network peering checklist, and the benchmark spreadsheet. Schedule Dedicated scoping on 2026-05-13. Daniel will send VPC diagram.
[43:18] Paul Chen: Sounds good. We'll review docs and loop in procurement and legal if everything matches.
[43:24] Maya Singh: I'll include a short section about KMS/HSM flows and an example of RBAC mappings to SAML groups.
[43:30] Jesse Carter: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with the packet and proposed calendar invite.
[43:36] Sara Vogel: Thanks.

[45:50] Call ended.
